I found this short explanation helpful.

The US Constitution protects you from "be[ing] compelled in any criminal case to be a "witness against himself," according to the text of the Fifth Amendment.

The important wording here is "witness against himself" and therein lies the most obvious situation in which you cannot "plead the Fifth" -- when the information being gathered is not testimonial in nature.

Further, statements that incriminate someone else would not be protected by the Fifth Amendment -- so if you are asked on the stand whether or not you saw your best friend commit some crime for which you are not charged or cannot be charged, you cannot refuse to answer on 5th Amendment grounds.
